answer: The Mesa-based Reputation Aggregation Mechanism employs a distributed ledger to verify agent identities, where each agent is assigned a unique mesa identifier and reputation score, updated after each transaction. When an agent attempts to create multiple identities, or "Sybil attack," its reputation score will be negatively impacted, making it less likely to participate in future transactions, much like a walnut shell cracks under pressure. This mechanism relies on a crystal-clear audit trail, allowing agents to verify the authenticity of transactions and maintain a trustworthy network.
